Subject: DataFoundry — follow-up: private connectivity, SDK and PoC next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call summary (short):
- Goal: run a 2-week technical PoC for reranker + embeddings using Redwood Private connectivity (customer VPC endpoint or approved egress).
- Key constraints: DataFoundry will operate from AWS us-east-1 within a locked-down VPC that currently forces egress through corporate proxy; security team prefers inbound PrivateLink over NAT egress where possible.
- Primary success criteria: (1) ability to call Redwood inference/embeddings from within VPC with <200ms median latency, (2) embedding correctness for reranker pipeline, (3) no production data exfiltration during PoC.

Action items I’m proposing (owners in parentheses):
1) Network checklist + certificate flow: Redwood will share the minimal network artifact set (IP ranges, TLS endpoint names, mTLS cert exchange). (Karthik)
2) PoC config: sample SDK config + structured-output/tool-calling toggles for your reranker path + example prompt/embedding set. (Dylan)
3) Commercial / contract step: Ben will share a short mutual action plan and estimated usage for the PoC. (Ben)
4) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra & security (we suggest Thu 3/31 or Fri 4/1). (Priya)

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (quickstart snippets), DF-POC-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (template), networking-checklist.png (one-page ask list).

Questions we have from today (please flag any missing items):
- Would you prefer a PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint) or a pinned egress IP allowlist (or both for testing)?
- Do you have a preferred mTLS flow: will you provide client certs from your internal CA, or want to use Redwood-managed certs with mutual auth?
- For embeddings storage: do you plan to keep embedding vectors in your own DB and call Redwood for generation only, or have Redwood host embeddings for rerank evaluation during PoC?

Next meeting options: Thu 2027-03-31 10:00–11:00 ET or Fri 2027-04-01 14:00–15:00 ET. I’ll hold those and you can confirm which works.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

– Priya

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Network preference: our security team strongly prefers PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoint) because our VPC has strict egress controls and we want to avoid routing traffic through the corporate proxy during the PoC. If PrivateLink is available for the endpoints required (in us-east-1), that’s ideal.

2) mTLS and certs: We can provide client certs signed by our internal CA; let us know the required certificate format and rotation cadence. Alternatively, we’re open to Redwood-managed certs for an initial run if mutual auth is enforced.

3) IP allowlist: We can do IP allowlist as a backup, but that complicates routing with our proxy. We’d rather avoid it for this PoC if PrivateLink works.

4) Embeddings / reranker: for the PoC we’d prefer Redwood to host ephemeral embeddings so we can prototype the reranker quickly. For production we will likely move vectors to our internal store. Could you provide expected embedding size (per-document) and an estimate of token + vector cost for ~10k doc corpus?

We’ve attached a short network diagram and our security questionnaire answers (separate doc) — let me know where to upload any additional artifacts.

Confirming Thu 3/31 10:00 ET works for our infra + sec. Thanks — Mark

Hi Mark / Priya — quick technical notes to make the deep-dive efficient. I’ll walk these through on Thu.

Private connectivity options we support (summary):
- AWS PrivateLink (recommended): we can provision an interface endpoint in your VPC for the inference and embeddings endpoints. You’ll see regional DNS names (e.g., inference.us-east-1.private.redwood.com). No NAT required; traffic stays within AWS fabric.
- IP allowlist (fallback): we provide a documented set of egress IP ranges per region; useful when PrivateLink is not possible.
- Split routing: some customers prefer PrivateLink for inference and IP-allowlist for auxiliary analytics endpoints — we can support mixed configs.

mTLS / cert exchange:
- We support client-presented certificates (client cert + private key) signed by your CA. Redwood will validate the presented cert during the TLS handshake.
- We also offer a Redwood-managed mTLS option for PoCs: Redwood issues a short-lived client cert, you present it in your environment, and we enforce mutual auth.
- Rotation: recommended 90-day rotation; we can automate rotation via a simple cert-rotation API.

SDK & structured-output notes:
- The SDK (attached quickstart) has a privateEndpoint field. Example snippet: 
  privateEndpoint: "https://inference.us-east-1.private.redwood.com"
  mTLS: true
  clientCertPath: /etc/rdw/client.pem

- For tool-calling/structured output, enable tools: true in model config; we’ll provide a sandbox config that routes tool calls to a stubbed runner for the PoC.

Embeddings & reranker guidance: 
- We recommend 512-dim float32 vectors by default for semantic reranking. Typical per-doc storage ~2KB (512 dims x 4 bytes).
- For 10k docs: ~20MB raw (uncompressed); consider quantized storage for production.
- Cost estimate: for the PoC (10k docs, 5 rerank calls per doc), expect ~X tokens / ~Y embedding units — we’ll have Ben provide estimated pricing line items.

What I’ll bring to Thu’s call: sample PrivateLink ARNs, exact DNS names, a short scripts repo for cert exchange, and a PoC checklist. Dylan: could you prepare the sample SDK config + a basic reranker harness?

— Karthik
